claims.value: Barton says his brigade was formed for attack by Ransom's orders and that two of his regiments were placed under officers of Ransom's choosing without formal orders to him; his covering letter protests being relieved of command and censured without charges, and Ransom's indorsement says the case will be remarked upon in his report. The frozen commanders are Major General Butler (US) and General Beauregard (CS); the live page gives Beauregard as Brigadier General.
claims.rationale: Barton's account is self-defence after his relief; Ransom's report is not inspected. Neither listed commander is shown directing the action in the inspected passages. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live result Indecisive. NPS says the Federals retired to their Bermuda Hundred lines; Humphreys says only some skirmishing ensued and Butler's troops returned to their intrenchments on the 10th. Barton says a large force gained his left and rear and that he retired across the morass to the position held before the assault.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Humphreys' 'only some skirmishing' and Barton's account of a close fight are not reconciled.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; for this campaign it summarizes Smith's, Gillmore's and Weitzel's reports and quotes Beauregard's reports and telegrams, so it is not independent of the Beauregard family. Butler's telegrams and Hagood's, Barton's and Beauregard's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Part 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
